market_summary: Wall Street opened higher as tech rebounded into Nvidia: S&P 500 +0.2% at ~7,665 and Nasdaq +0.4% at ~26,090 in the first hour, with oil -3% below $90 after markets shrugged off new US sanctions on Iran, and a soft Conference Board consumer confidence print (89.4 vs 90.2 expected, Expectations Index down to 68.2, a seven-month low) did little damage. Europe is heading into the close firmer (STOXX 600 +0.4% at ~657, DAX +0.6% at ~26,280) as the Iran risk premium eased, and Siemens Energy led our list at +3.2% on the EUR 10B+ steam-turbine sale reports. Robinhood (+6%) and Bloom Energy (+3.6%) were the only watchlist names moving more than 3%; Broadcom, Cloudflare, GE Vernova and Teradyne were flat. While you sleep the US session finishes (~6:00am AEST) and any Siemens Energy ad-hoc could land overnight; Wednesday brings July PCE (core expected 0.2% m/m, 3.3% y/y) and the second Q2 GDP estimate at 22:30 AEST, then Nvidia (consensus revenue ~$92B) and Salesforce report after the US close, roughly 6:30am AEST Thursday, which will set the tone for the whole AI complex on the list.

AMZN.reason: Slipped 0.4% to $260.92 in the first hour after closing Aug 24 at $262.07 (+1.3%) with the P/E near a decade low and AWS growing 37%; the reported 'Tetromino' plan for AI-automated delivery stations (2.5x throughput, pilot in 2028) is a long-dated margin lever, but the $220B capex plan, Bezos selling and state antitrust suits keep a lid on the multiple, so hold rather than chase.

AXOS.reason: Up 1.1% to $98.01 after announcing a dual listing on NYSE Texas, a cosmetic change; Benchmark's Aug 13 target hike to $120 (Buy) on above-peer growth and 17% ROE supports continuing to hold.

BABA.reason: The ADR is +0.35% at $118.88 as insiders lean in against the record HK$80B ($10.2B) placement: Jack Ma bought more than HK$600M of shares over consecutive days (SCMP) and chair Joe Tsai added another 720,000 Hong Kong shares on Tuesday, while BofA kept Buy/$172; the ~3.7% dilution and Michael Burry's exit still argue for waiting for the stock to base before adding.

ENPH.reason: Flat at $37.02 (-0.4%) after a 3.7% drop on Aug 24 with no fundamental catalyst; the AI assistant, IQ Battery C80 and a Dutch net-metering campaign are incremental, so stay on the sidelines until residential demand stabilizes.

FIGR.reason: Up 3.4% to $39.97 after EDX Markets integrated Figure's YLDS stablecoin as institutional collateral and a treasury asset, another distribution win on top of the Q2 beat (marketplace volume +132% to $4.3B) and Bernstein's $70 target; hold and let execution play out.

GOOGL.reason: Marginally lower at $347.24 (-0.2%) after Google Cloud launched Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services and for Legal, with Moody's plugging ratings data in via an MCP server and Weil signing on, a day after the Verizon partnership; these vertical enterprise wins support Cloud's +82% growth, Pixel production leaving China by 2027 trims tariff risk, and the post-Jeff-Dean dip remains a reasonable entry.

LDI.reason: Bounced 3% to $0.92 but remains below the $1 NYSE threshold after the formal non-compliance notice, with Goldman at Sell and a $1 target; exchange-compliance and dilution risk argue for reducing exposure.

META.reason: Up 1% to $564.58 in early trade as William Blair flagged a $100B+ opportunity in Meta's business AI agents, building on The Information's report that the Hatch consumer agent launches within weeks with a paid tier; but the California teen-addiction trial is in week two with testimony turning to Instagram's design (and a whistleblower saying Zuckerberg chose growth over kids' safety), the $942M New Mexico liability and $125-145B capex keep the stock ~29% off its high, so hold pending trial clarity.

MRVL.reason: Surged 6.2% to $243.47 in the first hour as Rosenblatt initiated at Buy with a $300 target and Susquehanna lifted its target to $265 (Wells Fargo $310 on Monday), all citing the Google warrant deal covering roughly $120B of custom AI product business through 2033; options still imply a ~12% move on Thursday's print (Fri ~6:30am AEST) against ~$2.71B revenue and $0.93 EPS consensus, and with the stock up ~160% YTD the bar is high, so hold through the report.

MU.reason: Up 1.8% to $926.78 after Monday's 5.8% drop on the CXMT/YMTC-for-Apple report, which Lynx Equity called an overreaction; Mizuho trimmed its target to $1,300 from $1,375 but kept Outperform, Barron's argues Micron will miss part of a 50% memory-price rise because of long-term contracts, HBM remains sold out through 2027, and expect volatility through Nvidia's print.

NFLX.reason: Up 1.7% to $81.39 after Wolfe Research raised its target to $95 from $84 (22x 2028 EPS of $4.41), arguing Q2's soft engagement was a release-schedule issue and that returning titles set up stronger second-half results; an ads-leadership reshuffle is worth watching but does not change the thesis, and at ~37% below the 52-week high with ad-tier and bundling optionality the valuation reset remains an add opportunity.

NVDA.reason: Up 1.5% to $211.66 in the first hour, snapping a seven-day losing streak, as Raymond James lifted its target to $352 from $330 and framed Nvidia's CPU franchise as strategically important in a server-CPU market it sees reaching $201B by 2030; the offset is OpenAI's Jalapeño chip, whose SemiAnalysis benchmarks claim more tokens per user and more throughput per kilowatt than Blackwell, with volume deployment in 2027. Options price a 5.4% (~$280B) move on Wednesday's report (Thu ~6:30am AEST) against ~$92B revenue consensus, so hold and reassess after the print.

RKT.reason: Eased 0.6% to $14.00 after Monday's FTC settlement of the Zillow/Redfin rental-listings case removed a legal overhang while letting the Zillow partnership run through 2030; the 10-year yield dipping to 4.65% helps at the margin, but after the earlier ~50% run the shares still look fully priced, so hold.

TSM.reason: Up 1.5% to $416.19 after Taipei shares rebounded 1.05% to NT$2,400; Apple's new M6 is described as a 2nm chip, the first mass-market 2nm silicon from TSMC's sole-source customer, and with 40%+ 2026 growth guidance, Xiaomi's 3nm Xring and the Sony image-sensor JV underlining demand breadth, the pullback from the June high remains a buying opportunity.

STRIPE.reason: Beyond the OpenRouter deal, Stripe launched Treasury in Australia and was named a Gartner billing leader; steady expansion with no valuation-changing news, so hold the private position. Marked at 2.27x cost: latest valuation ~$159B (2026-02) vs ~$70B at entry (https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/24/stripes-valuation-soars-74-to-159-billion/).

OPENAI.reason: OpenAI published first Jalapeño results: SemiAnalysis's InferenceX benchmark shows the Broadcom-co-designed inference chip delivering more tokens per user and more throughput per kilowatt than Nvidia Blackwell systems, with limited deployment from end-2026 and scale in 2027, a meaningful step toward lowering its compute bill; that offsets the Alabama AG subpoena and 15-state demand over the Hugging Face cyber-model breach and Altman's admission he overestimated AI's disruption pace. Private, so hold. Marked at 5.43x cost: latest valuation ~$852B (2026-08) vs ~$157B at entry (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/10/openai-reportedly-completed-a-7-billion-employee-tender-offer/).

headlines: MRVL +6% to $243 as Google's $120B warrant deal draws Rosenblatt ($300) and Susquehanna ($265) target hikes ahead of Friday 6:30am AEST earnings.
NVDA +1.5% to $211.66 on Raymond James's $352 target, but OpenAI's Jalapeño chip benchmarks claim more throughput per kilowatt than Blackwell; earnings Thu 6:30am AEST.
Consumer confidence slipped to 89.4 (90.2 expected) but stocks opened higher with 10-year at 4.65% and oil down 2.5%; NFLX +1.7% on Wolfe's $95 target.
BABA ADR +0.4% after Jack Ma bought HK$600M+ of shares and Tsai added 720k; Apple's 2nm M6 launch is a TSMC proof point, TSM +1.5%.
Conference Board consumer confidence fell to 89.4 in August (consensus 90.2), a seven-month low, with the Expectations Index sliding to 68.2.
Siemens Energy reportedly seeks EUR 10B+ for a majority stake in its steam-turbine unit, with CVC, EQT, Bain, Brookfield and KKR circling.
Oil fell ~3% to a one-week low below $90 as markets read new US Iran sanctions as economic, not military, pressure.
